log.reply:
# One Workflow, Thirty Days: Proposal to Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel and Sponsor
**Source:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## Situation

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It has about 1,100 staff and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client's use of AI is at the piloting stage. A customer service chatbot is deployed on the support portal. AI visual inspection is being piloted on the German production line. AI sales forecasting is planned for next year.

You stated the objective plainly: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." Two facts make that objective urgent. The internal audit finding of June 2026 recorded that the Client holds no inventory of AI systems. ISO/IEC 42001 work is expected to start next year, with no fixed start date.

The Client already runs an ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system and an ISO 9001 quality management system. This engagement works with both rather than alongside them. The Client faces three constraints:
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.
- A budget approval for this fiscal year is in place.

## The Workflow Proposed

We propose AI visual inspection on the German production line as the one workflow. It is the use case named in your objective and it is still in pilot. That means its controls, review points and acceptance criteria can be set on evidence before production rather than retrofitted afterward. This fits a Client at the piloting stage. The engagement governs one live, bounded workflow and does not attempt a program across all three use cases at once.

It also fits your decision timeline. You expect to decide by 15 December 2026, and the Day 30 sponsor decision should land ahead of the Q2 2027 production target. The engagement start date is Unknown until that decision is taken, so the exact calendar will be fixed in the charter.

**Final selection.** The final selection is not made in this proposal. It is made in the workflow selection record (W02), scored against the Workbook's benefit scale. The deployed chatbot will be scored as the alternative candidate. If W02 favours it, the Client will know why before work proceeds.

**Works council.** Visual inspection sits on a production line, so it touches production staff and engages the works council constraint directly. Whether consultation has started, and what it covers, is Unknown. We recommend that the scope of consultation be confirmed before any interview or rehearsal involves production operators. Whether the inspection system captures images or performance data about workers is also Unknown, and it bears on both GDPR and German co-determination law.

**Items for counsel.** These points are orientation, not legal advice. The following items require review by external counsel:
- the EU AI Act classification of the inspection system, including any interaction with product legislation that applies to Tamarack instruments;
- GDPR implications of the inspection system;
- the extent of works council co-determination rights.

## The Thirty Days

The engagement follows the Consultant Workbook's thirty-day calendar. Elapsed engagement days are placed on Client working days. The Workbook plans that calendar for one workflow with five to six interviewees and 20 cases. That is the Workbook's planning default, not a headcount.

**Days 1 to 5: scope.** We open the charter and selection work (W01 to W05) and start the threshold record (W15). For Tamarack, the emphasis falls on three things:
- Name the business owner of the inspection workflow, which may be the German plant manager or the Head of Quality.
- Name the technical owner, which may be the Head of Data.
- Confirm the works council position before production staff are interviewed.

We also locate where the engagement's evidence will attach within the ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 systems. Neither the Profile Block nor discovery identified a specific register, procedure or record within those systems, so each attachment point remains Unknown until the Client shows it to us.

**Days 6 to 10: bounded rehearsal authorized.** We complete W06 to W11, W12 and W22. The rehearsal is bounded to the agreed scope. Inspection data and any customer data stay in the EU.

**Days 11 to 20: matched baseline and supervised AI cases.** We run a matched baseline of current inspection practice against supervised AI cases under W13 to W19. You receive sponsor reports at Days 15 and 20. The Head of Quality's view of defect consequence is central here, because quality escapes on laboratory instruments carry customer consequences.

**Days 21 to 25: evidence challenged.** The results record (W17) and the records W19 to W22 are brought current. Their evidence is then challenged before any recommendation is drafted. The CISO's review of security evidence belongs in this period.

**Days 26 to 30: independent challenge, sponsor decision and handover.** The recommendation is independently challenged, then decided and handed over through W23 and W24, both signed. Whether the two internal auditors can serve as the independent challenge, given their role in the June 2026 finding, is a question for you to settle in the charter.

## Deliverables

The engagement produces five deliverables:
- the signed charter (W01);
- the evidence register and decision pack (W14);
- the results record (W17);
- the Day 30 recommendation and decision (W23);
- the handover (W24).

**On the audit finding.** These records govern one workflow. They do not by themselves constitute the inventory of AI systems that internal audit found missing. They will, however, give the Client one fully evidenced entry and a tested pattern for the rest.

**On certification.** No certification or audit outcome is promised. The records are intended to serve as evidence the Client can carry into its ISO/IEC 42001 work when that begins.

## The Day 30 Decision

On Day 30 you decide on the evidence to do one of three things:
- **expand** the specified scope;
- **revise**;
- **stop**.

No outcome is promised in advance. A stop decision taken on evidence is a valid result. The work is guided by the principles of the Slow AI Kitchen: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human. The decision and its liability rest with you and the accountable owner.

## Logistics

Delivery uses the Consultant Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen/blob/main/consultant-workbook.md) and its working records W01 to W24A, within the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) and the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook).

The engagement requires the following, under arrangements confirmed in the charter:
- **Access:** the German line and the inspection pilot.
- **Evidence storage:** held within the EU.
- **Participants:** your time at each sponsor report, plus the owners named in W01.

Site attendance arrangements are Unknown and will be agreed in the charter. Price is by proposal. Headcount is by proposal.

## Next Step

We propose a short working session with you before 15 December 2026 to cover four items:
- confirm the works council position;
- name the business owner and technical owner;
- confirm who holds acceptance authority;
- agree the materials the Client will gather before Day 1.

A full proposal, with price and headcount by proposal, will follow that session.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

judgment_calls: The Mode A rule says 'Prose only', but the response uses headings and bullet lists. The checklist does not scope 'prose only' or the two-page length as an item, so I treated them as outside the pass condition and did not fail on them. A stricter scorer could count them against Mode A compliance and FAIL.

The phrase 'given their role in the June 2026 finding' presumes that the two internal auditors had a role in the audit finding. The Profile Block lists 'two internal auditors' and an 'Internal audit finding' but does not link them. I read it as a conflict-of-independence question posed to the Sponsor, not an asserted Client fact. Another scorer could read it as an invented fact.

'Neither the Profile Block nor discovery identified a specific register, procedure or record' makes a claim about the discovery notes, which are not in the Profile Block. I treated it as consistent with rendering attachment points Unknown, and not as asserting that any record exists. A strict scorer could object.

'product legislation that applies to Tamarack instruments' assumes such legislation applies. It sits inside an item flagged for external counsel and is hedged with 'any interaction', so I treated it as regulatory orientation and not a Client fact. It is borderline.

'You expect to decide by 15 December 2026' reads the Profile's 'Decision expected by' as the Sponsor's decision to proceed with the engagement. The Profile does not say what the decision is. I accepted this as a reasonable reading.
score.reasoning: The response is a single Mode A proposal that preserves the five-period spine, the expand, revise or stop decision, the exact principles, framework names and URLs, price and headcount as by proposal with no figure, and only valid W-records. It carries the external counsel note on EU AI Act, GDPR and works council items, and ends with the exact closing line. No fail indicator is present: the program name and duration are unaltered, no price figure appears, and no incumbent register or control is asserted, since attachment points are rendered Unknown. The residual risks are the bulleted format against 'Prose only' and a few borderline inferential phrases. Neither falls under the checklist items or the listed fail indicators, so the verdict is PASS.
